items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the metropolitan
commuter transportation authority establishing and implementing a land
management policy
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7427

SPONSOR: MAYER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the metropol-
itan commuter transportation authority establishing and implementing a
land management policy

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To preserve the value of green space and flora to communities and to
provide for more thoughtful environmental land use in MTA rights-of-way
by imposing on the MTA new guidelines and processes for vegetation
management.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 requires the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the Long
Island Rail Road, and Metro-North Commuter Railroad Company to implement
a responsible land management policy that:

   (i) Promotes growth and conservation of native biodiversity and
   ecosystems;

   (ii) Prohibits clear-cutting and other broad-scale removals of
   vegetation;

   (iii) Establishes procedures for communication--in advance of
   vegetation management activities--with communities, other
   stakeholders affected by such activities, and with local officials
   and elected leaders;

   (iv) Require consultation with affected communities and stakeholders
   regarding vegetation management activities; and

   (v) Require consideration of any impacts on flooding by vegetation
   management activities.

Section 1 also defines certain terms.

Section 2 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In May of 2021, Metro North engaged in widespread and gratuitous clear-
cutting of vegetated land near the New Haven Line tracks and made other
land modifications that negatively affected adjacent properties. The
extent of the damage was dramatic and far in excess of what was neces-
sary to limit the hazards posed by trees that might fall. Consequences
of such actions to local communities included increased noise and air
pollution, elimination of visual barriers that provided privacy to those
living nearby, exacerbation of flooding risk, and damaged property
values. In addition, Metro North failed to give adequate notice to
affected communities.

Unfortunately, this is not an isolated incident. This legislation will
ensure that this type of destruction does not happen again in Mamaroneck
or anywhere else by requiring the MTA and its partners to engage in more
selective and thoughtful vegetation management and to be a good neighbor
by communicating and consulting with affected communities in advance.
The imposition of considerations for ecological sensitivity and flooding
will also enhance the benefits of the living environments in the rights-
of-way by promoting biodiversity and mitigating actions that may exacer-
bate flooding.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
The provisions of the bill shall take effect 180 days after becoming
law.

commuter transportation authority establishing and implementing a land and

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7427A

SPONSOR: MAYER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the metropol-
itan commuter transportation authority establishing and implementing a
land and vegetation management policy

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To preserve the value of green space to communities and to provide for
more thoughtful land use in MTA rights-of-way by requiring the MTA to
establish a land and vegetation management policy which includes new
guidelines and processes for vegetation management and community engage-
ment.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 requires the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the Long
Island Rail Road, and Metro-North Commuter Railroad Company to implement
a responsible land and vegetation management policy that:

(i) Includes guidelines for communication with local governments and
property owners affected by vegetation management activities;

(ii) Is consistent with commuter rail safety and efficiency guidelines;

(iii) Provides guidance for considering impacts on neighboring proper-
ties and communities, including a goal of minimizing impacts;

(iv) Provides that vegetation management activity impact assessment be
consistent with operational responsibilities of the commuter rail lines;

(v) Require meaningful prior written notice to impacted stakeholders;
and

(vi) Require consideration of any impacts on flooding as a result of any
vegetation or land management activities.

Section 2 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In May of 2021, Metro North engaged in widespread and gratuitous clear-
cutting of vegetated land near the New Haven Line tracks and made other
land modifications that negatively affected adjacent properties. The
extent of the damage was dramatic and far in excess of what was neces-
sary to limit the hazards posed by trees that might fall. Consequences
of such actions to local communities included increased noise and air
pollution, elimination of visual barriers that provided privacy to those
living nearby, exacerbation of flooding risk, and damaged property
values.  In addition, Metro North failed to give adequate notice to
affected communities.

Unfortunately, this is not an isolated incident. This legislation will
ensure that this type of destruction does not happen again in Mamaroneck
or anywhere else by requiring the MTA and its partners to engage in more

selective and thoughtful vegetation management and to be a good neighbor
by communicating and consulting with affected communities in advance.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
The provisions of the bill shall take effect 180 days after becoming
law.

AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the metropolitan

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7427B

SPONSOR: MAYER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the metropol-
itan commuter transportation authority establishing and implementing a
vegetation management policy

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To preserve the value of green space to communities and to provide for
more thoughtful vegetation management and handling of other activities
that impact neighboring properties in MTA rights-of-way by requiring the
MTA to establish a new policy which includes guidelines and processes
for vegetation management and community engagement.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 requires the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the Long
Island Rail Road, and Metro-North Commuter Railroad Company to implement
a policy for responsible management of vegetation and other activities
that impact neighboring communities that:

(i) Is consistent with applicable federal law;

(ii) Includes guidelines for communication with local governments and
property owners affected by vegetation management activities;

(iii) Is consistent with commuter rail safety and efficiency guidelines;

(iv) Provides guidance for considering impacts on neighboring properties
and communities, including a goal of minimizing impacts;

(v) Provides that vegetation management activity impact assessment be
consistent with operational responsibilities of the commuter rail lines;

(vi) Requires meaningful prior written notice to impacted stakeholders;
and

(vii) Requires consideration of any impacts on flooding as a result of
any activities covered by the policy.

Section 2 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In May of 2021, Metro North engaged in widespread and gratuitous clear-
cutting of vegetated land near the New Haven Line tracks and made other
land modifications that negatively affected neighboring properties. The
extent of the damage was dramatic and far in excess of what was neces-
sary to limit the hazards posed by trees that might fall.  Consequences
of such actions to local communities included increased noise and air
pollution, elimination of visual barriers that provided privacy to those
living nearby, exacerbation of flooding risk, and damaged property
values. In addition, Metro North failed to give adequate notice to
affected communities.


Unfortunately, this is not an isolated incident. This legislation will
ensure that this type of destruction does not happen again in Mamaroneck
or anywhere else by requiring the MTA and its partners to engage in more
selective and thoughtful vegetation management, and implementation of
other activities affecting neighboring properties, in a manner consist-
ent with its obligations to act as a good neighbor, and by communicating
with affected communities in advance.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
The provisions of the bill shall take effect 180 days after becoming
law.

summary: Relates to the metropolitan commuter transportation authority establishing and implementing a policy for responsible management of vegetation and other activities that impact neighboring properties in order to preserve the safety and efficiency of commuter rail operations by implementing guidelines for removal and management policies.
